03 Bugs found & fixed

Client-side-only auth

Fixed
BeforeGET /calendar (no session) → 200
AfterGET /calendar (no session) → 307 → /login

A logged-out visitor could open /calendar or any event page directly — the server returned the page and only redirected later in the browser. Fix: moved the session into a cookie and added a server-side middleware.ts guard. Re-verified in the browser (Flow 8).

Favicon 404 console error

Fixed
BeforeGET /favicon.ico → 404 (console error)
Afterconsole clean · all requests 200/304

Every page logged a 404 for a missing favicon. Fix: added app/icon.svg. Re-tested — the browser no longer requests /favicon.ico and the console is completely clean.

Also noted (by design, not a bug): “Request edit” confirms the request but does not yet regenerate — the feedback→pipeline wiring is deliberately out of MVP scope.

04 Evidence

05 Reflection

Building this the agentic way changed where the time went. Instead of hand-clicking through the app, I described the outcome I wanted — “test every flow like a real user, prove it with screenshots” — and let Claude drive the browser, watch the console and network, and report back ranked by severity.

The most useful part wasn't the passing flows; it was being forced to see the app the way a skeptical judge would — an unhappy path I'd never clicked, a route that loaded when it shouldn't have. The honest moment came early: the repo had no app to test yet. Rather than fake a report, we built the minimal dashboard first, then tested the real thing.

The lesson: agentic testing is only as truthful as the evidence it produces. Screenshots, console logs, and a file that actually appears on disk keep it honest — and “it looks right in the code” is never the same as “I drove it and watched it work.”
